origin: Credited to William Playfair of Scotland, who first used it in his 1786 book The Commercial and Political Atlas. The line chart debuted in the same book.
whenToUse: You compare the sizes of items with each other.
You compare on the same scale while changing the period.
whenNotToUse: Change over time (use a line chart).
Shares of a whole (use a donut chart or a stacked bar chart).
Emphasizing a single number (use a KPI card).

alternatives.name: Stacked Bar Chart
alternatives.reason: Also showing the makeup inside each bar.

alternatives.name: Line Chart
alternatives.reason: Seeing change along an ordered axis.

accessibility: Each item is a list entry with a name and value, so the numbers are read as they are.
The bars are aria-hidden decoration, and color carries no meaning.
With reduced motion, the length transition turns off.
